claims.text: The log opens: '7 Nov 75 (1035Z) - Received a call from the 341st Strategic Air Command Post (SAC CP), saying that the following missile locations reported seeing a large red to orange to yellow objects M-l, L-3, LIMA and L-6. The general object location would be 10 miles south of Moore, Montana, and 20 miles east of Buffalo, Montana. Commander and Deputy for Operations (DO) informed.'

claims.source: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 8 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The interception sequence is in the log's own words. '8 Nov 75 (0753Z) - J330 unknown 0753. Stationary/seven knots/12,000... two F-106, GTF, SCR 0754. NCOC notified.' '8 Nov 75 (0820Z) - Lost radar contact, fighters broken off at 0825.' '8 Nov 75 (0905Z) - From SAC CP: L-sites had fighters and objects; fighters did not get down to objects.' '8 Nov 75 (0915Z) - From SAC CP: From four different points: Observed objects and fighters; when fighters arrived in the area, the lights went out; when fighters departed, the lights came back on; to NCOC.'

claims.source: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE LOG RECORDS ITS OWN NEGATIVES, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH TIER 1. After the 7 Nov 1327Z entry it notes: 'all this time, surveillance has not been able to detect any sort of track except for known traffic.' On 9 Nov 0320Z the FAA watch supervisor reported five air carriers in the vicinity and United Flight 157 reported seeing a meteor, arc welder's blue in colour. On 12 Nov 0251Z: 'Reported that both objects have disappeared. Never had any joy (contact) on radar.'

claims.source: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 19 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The log's final entry is marked in the original as the last pertaining to these incidents: '19 Nov 75 (1327Z) - SAC command post report UFO observed by FSC & a cook, observed object travelling NE between M-8 and M-l at a fast rate of speed. Object bright white light seen 45 to 50 sec following terrain 200 ft off ground. The light was two to three times brighter than landing lights on a jet.'

The Black Vault's landing page for OASD FOIA case 97-F-1677, released September 1997, describes records of numerous unidentified craft over Malmstrom AFB in November 1975 that could not be intercepted by multiple F-106 fighters. THE PAGE ITSELF REPRODUCES NO DOCUMENT TEXT, so the non-interception claim is corroborated here by the NORAD log rather than by that page.

desc: THE STRONGEST SINGLE ARTEFACT IN THE NUCLEAR STRAND, BECAUSE IT IS A WORKING LOG RATHER THAN A REPORT WRITTEN FOR ANYBODY. Between 7 and 19 November 1975 the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log at Malmstrom AFB recorded a run of reports from Minuteman launch control facilities and launch facilities across the 341st Strategic Missile Wing's field: objects over M-1, L-3, Lima and L-6; an object illuminating a site driveway at the Harlowton launch control facility; K-1 watching a very bright object through 10x50 binoculars; L-1 reporting a tubular black object issuing from another object; height-finder radar picking up between two and seven objects at 10,000 to 13,000 feet; two F-106s scrambled; radar contact lost and the fighters broken off; and, from four separate points, the report that when the fighters arrived the lights went out and when the fighters departed the lights came back on. The log is even-handed in a way an advocate's document would not be: it records that surveillance could detect no track except known traffic, that an airline crew reported a meteor, and that on 12 November the controllers 'never had any joy (contact) on radar'. It ends with an entry marked, in the original, as the last entry pertaining to these incidents.

timeline.label: Two F-106s scrambled over the Malmstrom missile field; radar contact lost
timeline.text: The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 8 November 1975: height-finder personnel picked up objects at 10,000 to 13,000 feet on track J330; two F-106s were scrambled at 0754Z; at 0820Z 'Lost radar contact, fighters broken off at 0825'; at 0905Z 'L-sites had fighters and objects; fighters did not get down to objects'; and at 0915Z, from four different points, 'when fighters arrived in the area, the lights went out; when fighters departed, the lights came back on'.

unverified: The larger FOIA compilation from which this log was extracted. The pages carry stamps 450, 451 and 452 and a control number 000974 over the release line of Terrence C. James, Colonel, USAF, Director of Administration. At least 449 pages of that compilation have never been seen by this board.
Two further named men, SSgt Joseph M. Chassey and Lt Col Robert Peisher (USAF Ret.), appear in Hastings's Malmstrom 1975 material and their basis was not established by this pass.
